$comment: MC-4801 machining centre main spindle twin. Expected cutting power from the Kienzle specific cutting force of the cut the CNC reports, expected temperatures and thermal growth from the mean speed, defect frequencies from the bearing geometry; the machine sends only what it measures.

identification.description: Main spindle of a 3-axis vertical machining centre (job shop, steel and aluminium parts)
identification.spindle: Motor spindle, 230 mm housing, built-in motor, oil-air lubricated angular contact ball bearings (70 mm bore at the front)
identification.tool_interface: HSK-A63 (DIN 69893) with automatic clamping set (disc spring pack, drawbar, hydraulic release)
identification.cooling: Water-cooled housing and motor from the machine's spindle chiller
identification.cnc: CNC with an MTConnect agent or an OPC UA server for machine tools (OPC 40501-1)

spindle.source: GMN milling spindles page (gmn.de), HCS series table, line HCS 230 - 20000 / 40. Above the base speed the twin takes constant power up to n max: assumption: typical value, replace with the S1 power curve of your spindle's data sheet (GMN's sister HCS 230 - 20000/25 shows power falling near n max)

drive.source: Idle (no-load) power = p0 + p1 (n/1000) + p2 (n/1000)^2 from bearing friction and windage, and the motor efficiency at load: assumption: typical value, replace with an air-cut test of this spindle at five speeds at commissioning

material.name: C45 (1.0503) steel, normalised, ISO P
material.source: Kienzle coefficients kc1.1 and mc of the work material: assumption: typical value, replace with your tool maker's material data (they vary with the material and its heat treatment)

bearing.type: angular contact ball bearing, 70 mm bore (7014 size), hybrid (ceramic balls)
bearing.source: Bore 70 mm from the GMN milling spindles page (gmn.de), HCS series table, line HCS 230 - 20000 / 40. Ball count, ball diameter and contact angle: assumption: typical value, replace with the bearing maker's data or its published defect frequency factors

thermal.source: Expected bearing temperature = coolant inlet + c0 + c1 x (mean speed / 1000 rpm); motor = coolant inlet + m0 + m1 x mean power (kW); Z thermal growth of the spindle nose = g0 + g1 x (mean speed / 1000 rpm). assumption: typical value, replace with the spindle thermal test (ISO 230-3) and a fit on a few weeks of healthy data of this spindle

vibration.source: Envelope acceleration at the front bearing BPFO = e0 + e1 x (n / n max) (g); 1x vibration velocity = v0 + v1 x (n / 10,000 rpm)^2 (mm/s). assumption: typical value, replace with the baseline learnt with balanced tools on this spindle

clamping.source: Roehm HSK brochure, HSK A63 clamping set: clamping force 18 kN, actuating force 6 kN. The alarm fractions in twin_model.limits are assumptions

cooling.source: Spindle chiller flow, inlet set point and oil-air supply pressure: assumption: typical value, replace with the spindle maker's installation data

balance.source: Balance quality grade G 2.5, commonly applied to machine tool spindles and tool assemblies (ISO 21940-11): assumption: typical value, replace with the grade in your tool balancing specification

demo.note: Demo only: one real second is ten machine seconds. The stand-in machine runs a four-operation part program in a loop (roughing, face milling, pocketing, finishing, each 90 machine seconds plus a 10 s tool change); the edge keeps 5-minute mean speed and power.

program.source: The stand-in part program (tools, cutting data, tool masses with HSK holder): assumption: typical value, replace with your CAM data; the CNC sends the values of the active cut

points.label: Cutting diameter of the active tool
Number of teeth of the active tool
Rake angle of the active tool
Mass of the tool assembly (tool + HSK holder)
Axial depth of cut of the active operation
Radial width of cut of the active operation
Axial thermal growth of the spindle nose
Envelope acceleration at the front bearing outer-race frequency
Clamping force measured at the last tool change
Highest shock at the spindle nose, last 24 h
Shocks above the crash threshold since the last rebuild

limits.source: Alarm limits: assumption: typical value, replace with your fleet statistics, the spindle maker's limits and the clamping set maker's minimum clamping force

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

bearing_damage.name: Front bearing damage (outer-race spall)
bearing_damage.symptoms: envelope at the outer-race frequency grows, front bearing runs hotter than the speed model predicts

lubrication_starvation.name: Oil-air lubrication starved (blocked line, empty tank)
lubrication_starvation.symptoms: oil-air pressure low, both bearings hotter than the model, vibration still normal

cooling_failure.name: Spindle cooling lost (chiller, hose, blocked jacket)
cooling_failure.symptoms: cooling flow low, motor much hotter than its load explains, spindle grows more than the thermal model

tool_imbalance.name: Unbalanced tool assembly (or chips on the HSK taper)
tool_imbalance.symptoms: vibration at 1x spindle speed well above the balanced baseline, bearings normal

clamping_force_loss.name: Clamping force loss (disc springs fatigued, clamping set dry)
clamping_force_loss.symptoms: clamping force at tool change falls below the clamping set's nominal value

tool_wear.name: Worn cutting tool
tool_wear.symptoms: spindle power above the Kienzle cutting power of the same cut, everything else normal

spindle_crash.name: Spindle crash (collision of tool or head)
spindle_crash.symptoms: shock above the crash threshold, then 1x vibration up (bent tool or holder, damaged taper)
